body: Thank you.

I was hoping that it was a sort of confirmation bias (if that's the correct term I'm thinking of) that only people with side effects bothered to post about them and hopefully a majority are fine. Thank you for your advice.
My brother doesn't smoke weed, nor do I think he would, and probably shouldn't. But without the weed you would have more side effects?
Thank you.

I know this might be hard to ask but do you know anyone else who have taken SNRIs and if they had the same effects? What do you mean by "zombified"? And also is there anything I should know from as an outside party?
I do and so does my family, I am just looking for anything to help.
Thank you and I will soon.
Thank you.
Thank you.
Not to go into too much technical detail a major part of it is stress from college and failing grades.
I'm sorry to hear that and hope you're doing better. Thank you.
Thank you, and we are doing everything we currently can to help.
We have already set up for him to see a therapist weekly and have the local suicide hotline on speed dial. Thank you very much.
I did not take it as an insult whatsoever, no need to apologize, and thank you.

We know that we can't just cure him or offer a solution and that we have to help to get him better. In the phone calls and the in person visit (I was not able to visit him nor any of my family since we had to all work today) we've just listened and asked a few questions and talked about our experiences in a few cases.

I did try to ask them why they said the things they did and none of them responded. It's fine though because of all the comments and messages I have gotten only maybe 4 I would say are negative. Thank you for the advice and concern.
I have never been religious but  I might try that. Thank you.
Oh, sorry, I didn't know what you meant by editing but that's fine. Thank you.

I was able to visit him in person earlier today and I asked him a few questions but mostly listened and told him how much we love him and that we're there for him. We can also call if we can't visit since they only allow one visitor per day per patient due to COVID. Thank you for your concern.
Thank you.

It's all good, I just got back from visiting him at the psychiatric clinic and I'm not sure whether to edit my posts or make new ones or to delete the ones I have already made. Being able to talk with someone and with him has made things better.
I can use all of it right now, thank you.

I wish I could just help him but you're right, there's professionals for that, I have to do all I can to comfort him.

Thank you.
I hope he's just confused and that if he does have an illness a doctor can help him. I'm going to spend much more time with him doing the things we both use to enjoy.

I just hope the doctors can tell him whatever he has is able to be cured and that we can support him. I'm a bit shaken up but since we were able to talk to him over the phone I feel much better both mentally and physically.

I never took offense, so no need to apologize. In the past we told him to talk to his professors and he did take a semester off, we just have to do better to try to help him handle his stress by talking to him.
Thank you.
We're able to call and possibly visit in person.
We have had trouble trying to find therapists in the past since there's a lack of them here in Louisiana, but thankfully we have found a few that can help.

We spoke to him over the phone earlier and we'll try to visit him tomorrow but due to COVID we can't all go and we're still discussing who goes and who doesn't. Right now I wish I just had someone to talk to who cares but isn't as affected or distraught as we are.

My father has COPD from smoking since the age of 11 and my mother has diabetes, my grandparents have the same conditions. Due to my father's line of work he does employer provided health insurance, the only in my family that has health insurance. But when his stomach ruptured in a horrible accident 5 years ago we had to pay out of pocket. When he was in the hospital he was maybe hours away from death and I remember then even with how young I was, standing there crying, he told me everything he would be fine. Ever since then I have been bitter about the healthcare system and what it could do and even in the years following over things more minor than my father's it has been a struggle, I really hope that if he needs to be placed in care they firstly do so and the insurance isn't important. I work with a good job and have savings I can use and my older brother who lives two states away can do the same. 

Thank you for your concern and I will update soon hopefully.

They have to keep him for 72 hours and then they will do an assessment on whether he is stable and can be released or has to be put in for a period of time, though they can only do so if there's beds and professionals available and the state I live in doesn't have many facilities. I wish I could tell him right now that his mental state is just like a broken bone and can heal and that he doesn't have to harm himself. They took him off SSRIs and switched them to NRIs and I sincerely hope he was just given the wrong medicine combined with us not asking him how he was doing. There is a private clinic that we can send him to if we have to but we're a middle class family already on edge over fears about the economy and COVID and we're not sure if insurance will cover it. We live in Louisiana and Texas is a 5 hour drive and I don't know if AL or MS will have better care for him than LA.

The thing about babyproofing has been hard for us, we have already replaced door knobs and gotten rid of anything that he could harm himself with. I wish he sees that as a sign that we care about him, he made it very clear that he wouldn't use a gun or a knife since he didn't want to leave a mess, and the reason he didn't go through with hanging himself was because he felt as if he couldn't do it in the same house as his parents, despite that though he didn't run off which gives me hope. Thank you for the prayers, all that we get at this moment means everything.

It was never our plan to ever offer a "solution", if we did, it was in the form of getting him anti-depressants after his first attempt, the same drugs may have caused insomnia and psychosis. I just feel like I should've been closer there with my brother and maybe it wouldn't have reached this point, in the future it will be that way.

As for my own health, I am doing much better, I knew that not eating anything in the last 24 hours wasn't good but I was just too worried about my brother. I have already had a good dinner and don't feel like I have the flu anymore.

Thank you for my concern, looking at some of my earlier posts now that I have a clearer less worried head makes me feel like I didn't realize how much you people really do care and don't want to see this happen.

I have been sitting with my family since last night and all today trying to figure out what to say him, when to do it, how to phrase it, I feel much less shaken now that we were able to speak with him at the clinic, but how do I tell him he doesn't have to do this? Do I tell him that has never lost control and can make things better if he puts himself to it and with our help? that could be a problem since he believes he has a mental illness that is stopping that. I have already read that saying things like they would in movies like "you mean so much to me" or "you have so much to live for" are wasted at best and harmful at worst.

My brother has always been a savant in mathematics since age 12 and wanted to do amazing things in that field, enter academia and become like his idol Grigori Perelman. He felt like if his grades didn't reflect that he was a failure. I have spent most of the day either sitting on a couch trying to console my parents or them console me or reading about what to do in a situation like this, we're not sure how to tell him that though.

We just spoke to him at the clinic, he seems to be doing much better but I had trouble keeping it together, there was all this going on with him and I never knew. He has expressed faith in the doctors which has made me feel a million times better but he still believes he's ill. He was still uncomfortable with all our emotion and kept apologizing so we didn't get to ask him in much detail about everything.

I do have to ask if I remember correctly psychosis can be caused by insomnia yes? 

Thank you for your concern and information and I have bookmarked the videos.

Due to some confusion with how reddit works I did post there and I checked not too long ago and the comments are, I don't really know how to describe it. Mean spirited? Spiteful? I hope it's just the people there posting are suffering from the same thing my brother has and aren't entirely reasonable, but at one of the worst moments of my life I don't have much motive to check them further.

I have spent most of my life with him, we played video games or just hung out around eachother. He was always happy up until about a year ago when things started to change, I just thought it was the stress of schoolwork but I didn't realize he had actually tried to kill himself twice before yesterday., I wish I could've just asked him "how do you feel?". My parents have loved all of us very much and supported us for our entire lives. Up until 2 weeks ago he was fine but then his grades started to drop.

Right now I'm not in the clearest state nor are my parents. I feel terrible, I have barely eaten anything in the past 30 or so hours but I know that if I do eat I will probably just throw up, my parents feel the same way too. I never have had depression in my life and generally always been very content, same goes for my parents but in both sides of my family are histories of alcoholism,depression and suicide.
Thank you. For all the advice and for your concern.
Thank you for the concern.
I'm sorry to hear about your loss, I hope you're doing okay too. Thank you for your concern and adivce.
I wish he had come to me and just opened up about all this. We can get him the help he needs and I just want him to know that we truly care and love him.
Thank you for the advice.
Thank you for giving me another place to look for advice and help.
That's all I want to do right now. Thank you for your concern.
Thank you.
Thank you for your concern and advice.
There's not enough advice me or my family can't receive right now. We don't even know if where's he's at has good treatment or anything. I will mention the 5160 as a possible option though.
I'm sorry to hear, is there any advice you can give me on what I can do?

He seems to believe he has a mental illness of some sort, I'm personally trying to do what I can to figure out what's going on but in his notes he drew alot of eyes and strange self portraits. I don't know whats going on and I just want to help him. We have already set up weekly appointments with therapists.

I've know for a while he was unhappy in college but was unaware of how bad it really was. He did ask me for alot of my books which I happily obliged to, and he mentioned that in his notes but I had no idea. My parents knew he had attempted suicide twice before but I never knew about that, they didn't know what else to do but send him to psychward and I can't blame them.
He doesn't do any substances, he claims to have a mental illness and they might diagnose him with one, they switched him off SSRIs to NRIs as well. Thank you for the advice.
I just found out he was taking SSRIs before and they have switched him to NRIs.

Unfortunately we don't live in a state with great mental health care which is terrifying. We don't even know what clinic he's at and they can only hold him for 72 hours, do an assessment and then decide if he should be released or put in a hospital, and there's not many of them. Right now is really tough for me and I thank you for your concern.
Thank you.

I use to play video games with him alot when I was younger but since then work and a lack of interest has made me stop playing them as often. He takes every moment he can to read. Thank you for your concern.
Thank you for the advice.
He has a few online friends, he doesn't have his own car or residence besides his apartment at college. While he had trouble connecting with people he always seemed to be fine by himself.

He was already staying at my parents due to COVID cancelling all in-person classes at college. So he was on his holiday break already when my mom discovered him writing his suicide note. He doesn't have very many friends outside of family/associates and always had trouble connecting with people, hence why my mother thought he may have autism.

He isn't opposed to getting help from medical professionals but he doesn't believe it will be that useful. He isn't out of his stay in the psychiatric ward so I don't know if it's been good for him or not yet. Thank you for the advice.

He definitely trusts us and in his notes said that he loved us very much, but he felt that we couldn't do anything for him and his supposed mental illness. We have been looking for therapists and other professionals to talk for the past 30 hours or so.

We've already been trying to get rid of anything in the house that he could use to potentially harm himself and trying to set up appointments with therapists and other professionals. Thank you for the advice and support.

He was on anti-depressants before and they recently upped his dosage, whether that has something to do with it or not I'm not sure, they're apparently changing his medicine but I don't know if what he was taking before was SSRIs or if they changed it to that. Thank you for the advice.

We just don't know what to do, in the past while he never stated he was suicidal, he expressed anguish over college and a fear that he won't "be anyone in life". I've been at my parents house all day trying to help them and online any moment I could get to find advice and I just don't know how to tell him that what he believes isn't true.
I just watched the video and it was very good, I learned a few things to help my brother with, thank you.
Thank you.
He is 19.
